speaker: Doctor
text: I notice you have double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness. To understand the severity and location of your issue, how long have these symptoms been present, and do you experience any drooping eyelids or slurred speech?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pattern of fluctuating weakness and diplopia worsened by activity is highly suggestive of a neuromuscular junction disorder. Have you noticed any difficulty swallowing, speaking clearly, or breathing deeply recently? REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, Electrolytes, Creatine_Phosphokinase.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal blood work rules out myasthenia gravis and Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome. Given your specific symptoms of double vision triggered by looking up/down, plus proximal weakness in the arms and legs, do you have a history of thyroid eye disease or any recent head trauma? REQUEST TEST: Thyroid_Stimulating_Hormone, Thyroxine.

speaker: Doctor
text: With thyroid function and standard blood work normal, we need to rule out mechanical issues or specific ocular motility disorders. Did you notice any recent head trauma or a history of thyroid eye disease, and are you experiencing any pain behind your eyes? REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Brain_with_Ocular_Protocols

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since your symptoms are symmetrical and triggered by specific eye movements without pain, this points toward a restrictive myopathy rather than a neuromuscular junction issue. Have you noticed any trouble rising from a seated position or climbing stairs due to hip girdle weakness, and do you experience any neck stiffness or trouble turning your head? REQUEST TEST: Creatine_Kinase, Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis with ocular and proximal muscle involvement.
